params.body:
## What

Three things in the Studio.

### 1. Curate's first screen is gentells.com's front page, and editors arrange it there

The overview was a queue beside a column of counts. It is now the front page drawn the way a reader gets it, in the site's own faces and colours: the lead post, the six under it, the six trends, the reports, with a switch between the member's and the visitor's page. Beside it, a tray of what waits.

- Placing is the decision. A proposed trend goes onto one of the six places (approve and order in one move); a post in review goes onto the lead (publish and pin) or live at its date. While a decision is held the page shows it in place, in pencil, with what it would push off.
- On the page: pin another post as the lead or let the newest lead again; drag the trends into order or move one up; hide a trend and the next in line moves up; take a post off.
- Every change ends in a message with Undo, which puts back exactly what was there. Only the latest change stays undoable, so an older undo can never restore a state the later changes no longer start from.
- The placement rules (`src/frontpage.js`) mirror the site's HomeController and are tested.

Needs the pipeline PR (trend order, lead pin, exact restore). The site follows the pinned lead in its own PR.

### 2. Writing starts calmer

- A new piece opens wide: the conversation in the middle, "Open a blank page" for whoever knows what to write, and the starters from this week's signals as cards with the numbers behind them. "See all" opens a browser over every starter, with search, a period, and endless paging from the pipeline.
- The sheet grows in stages instead of all at once: the views line, the standfirst and the margin keep their room from the start so the line being typed never moves, the sources arrive once there is a sentence, and the opportunity, elements and cover once the piece has a body.
- Writing tools where the text is: a + beside an empty paragraph (image, heading, quote, list), a bar on a selection (bold, italic, link, heading, quote, list), and Ctrl or Cmd with B, I and K.
- "Subheading" replaces "standfirst" as the placeholder.

### 3. One colour, and type that reads

- The Studio's colour is pencil yellow, from the header rule to the favicon. Text in it uses a darker ink (5.6:1 on white), and a filled yellow button is lettered in ink. Warnings use the danger red; aqua stays with the Observatory and no longer appears here, Curate included.
- Body text in IBM Plex Sans, headlines in Fraunces. Inside the drawn front page, gentells.com's own Newsreader.
- Write and Curate in the header, and Curate's sections, are words with a pencil underline for the current one. Starting a piece is "+ New piece" as text, not a filled button. Delete in the editor is quiet until hovered; Format and Brand choose from a menu.

## Tests

`npm test`: 34 pass (placement rules, staging, formatting helpers). `npm run build` passes. Checked in a browser against a local pipeline: placing a trend, pinning a lead, dragging, undo, the writing stages, the starter browser, the format bar, at desktop and phone width.

New dependencies: `@fontsource-variable/ibm-plex-sans`, `@fontsource-variable/fraunces`, `@fontsource-variable/newsreader`.
